Thank you, Madam Chair. This report is seeking approval for the administration to submit two applications for round two of the disaster mitigation and adaptation fund or DMAF program.

As outlined in the report, the DMAF is a national competitive and merit-based contribution program, intended to support infrastructure projects designed to mitigate current and future climate-related risks and disasters triggered by natural hazards such as floods, wildfires, droughts, and seismic events.
The proposed applications are for 45.2 million in eligible costs for expansion of the city's flood control strategy and 30.5 million for the park and green space upgrades.
If successful, the DMAF program would provide 40% of eligible costs for selected projects.

For all submitted projects, the city's share of funding would already exist or in the case of the civic water conservation, the city's share could be funded through a green loan based on the anticipated savings from the implementation.

This report is requesting approval of the terms of reference for the project management processes audit.
The city spends millions of dollars under taking large and complex capital and operational projects,
and it is important that the city has strong project management practices in place.
If effective project management helps the city meet business objectives,
satisfy public expectations, resolve problems and issues,
optimize the use of city resources and manage change better.
In accordance with the approved audit plan,
the independent office of the city auditor has come in the audit of project management processes.
The objective of this audit is to assess if the city has strong project management processes
to ensure that projects are completed timely within budget and meet project deliverables and public expectations.
This includes the evaluation of the management of vendor contracts.
The area is to be covered within the audit will include comparing current project management processes
against best practices, comparing economic efficiencies, project processes and documentation,
project governance, vendor management, staff training and project reporting.
The office will review the current framework and practices for managing projects,
review records, conduct verification procedures, and select a sample of key projects for assessing against project management best practices.
Subject to the availability of data and information, the office will compare the city's project management processes
and practices with other municipalities to assess whether city is at power with other municipalities in terms of managing its projects.
A detailed audit report will be submitted to the Standing Policy Committee on Finance at the November 2023 public meeting.
The detailed terms of reference is attached to the appendix.
